title: Instruction Protocols: Moral Licensing, Instrumental Apology and Insincerity Aversion: Taking Immanuel Kant to the Lab
author: Elias Khalil

steps_raw.instruction: Instruction Protocols: Moral Licensing, Instrumental Apology and Insincerity Aversion: Taking Immanuel Kant to the Lab Elias L. Khalil and Nick Feltovich § The instructions were seen on screen and on paper for Part 1-- the instructions were read aloud for Part 1. Participants were then able to ask questions to ensure they understood the task. § For Part 2 and Bonus, everything was written on screen, and was not provided on paper. Also, the instructions were not read aloud. Participants could ask questions to ensure they understood the task. § We did not offer practice rounds. We did not collect demographic data. We did not conduct interviews after the sessions. [hard copy, read aloud, and on-screen--Part 1, all treatments] Thank you for participating in today’s experiment. Please read these instructions carefully. If you have a question at any time during this experiment, please raise your hand and the experimenter will answer your question individually. Please do not communicate with anyone else – either aloud or via any device – during this experiment. This experiment consists of two parts. Please note that you will be paid for only one of these two parts. This will be decided by a coin toss at the end of the experiment. If the coin lands heads all participants are paid for the first part while if it lands on tails all participants are paid for the second part. All participants additionally receive $10 for completing the experiment. You will be randomly matched to one of the other participants in this room. One of you will be randomly assigned to a role of “proposer,” and the other will be a “responder.” You and the person matched to you will remain unknown to each other throughout this experiment. The proposer and responder will have the opportunity to split $10 between them. Proposer’s decision: The proposer chooses a proposed split of the $10 between him-/herself and the responder. The following splits are possible: $10 for the proposer and $0 for the responder $9 for the proposer and $1 for the responder $8 for the proposer and $2 for the responder $7 for the proposer and $3 for the responder $6 for the proposer and $4 for the responder $5 for the proposer and $5 for the responder $4 for the proposer and $6 for the responder $3 for the proposer and $7 for the responder $2 for the proposer and $8 for the responder $1 for the proposer and $9 for the responder $0 for the proposer and $10 for the responder Responder’s decision: The responder is informed about the proposer’s choice, and then decides to accept or reject the proposal. --If the responder decides to accept, both proposer and responder split the $10 as proposed. --If the responder decides to reject, both proposer and responder receive $0. Please follow the instructions on your screen for additional information. [on-screen only--Part 2]

[Baseline] Here you repeat playing the same game as in Part 1. You will play the same role you played in Part 1, but you are matched to a different person. [The instructions are then identical to Part 1] [Known apology] Here you repeat playing the same game as in Part 1. You will play the same role you played in Part 1, but you are matched to a different person. [The instructions are identical to Part 1] [Prior to the proposer making his or her offer, the proposer gets the following message] You also have a choice of sending, along with your proposal, the following message to the responder: "Sorry for the proposal." If you decide to send the message, the responder will receive it at the same time as he/she receives your proposal. If you do not send the message the responder will not receive a message. [only if the proposer has sent apology message, responder receives this message along with the split proposal] The proposer matched with you, at the same time as making his/her proposal, decided to send you this message: "Sorry for the proposal.” [Unknown apology] Here you repeat playing the same game as in Part 1. You will play the same role you played in Part 1, but you are matched to a different person. [The instructions are identical to Part 1] [After the proposer makes his or her offer (but before it is sent to the responder) the proposer gets the following message] Your proposal now is recorded and cannot be rescinded. However, there is one difference: you have a choice of sending, along with your proposal, the following message to the responder: "Sorry for the proposed offer." If you decide to send the message, the responder will receive it at the same time as he/she receives your proposed offer. If you do not send the message the responder will not receive a message. [only if the proposer has sent apology message, responder receives this message along with the split proposal] The proposer matched with you, after making his/her proposal, decided to send you this message: "Sorry for the proposal.” [on-screen only—Part 3, all treatments] [Responder receives this message] You have an additional selection to make. You can permit the experimenter to give unconditionally an additional amount, between $0 and $5, to the proposer. The amount can be $0, $1, $2, $3, $4, $5. The proposer will be aware of the amount even if you select to give $0. [Proposer receives this message] The responder can also decide to allow the experimenter to give you unconditionally an additional amount, between $0 and $5. Please wait while they make this decision.
